blockers: target_env_data_space_ceiling_stale_cache: the deployed daily runtime answered payment.request ui.contract.v2 with 403 for an enrolled operator (uid 210) because `_sc_data_company_ids()` decided the data-purpose realm from `res.users.has_group`, a `tools.ormcache` helper. The fixture writes through `odoo shell`, which never signals cache invalidation, so the long-lived worker kept its previous membership answer and resolved an empty authorized-company set; the same window would have kept serving a just-revoked principal. Readback proof on the deployed runtime: HTTP `has_group` returned false while the persisted relation carried the row, and flipped to true immediately after a `clear_cache()` + `signal_changes()` from the shell. Repaired in branch at the owning layer (`res_users.py` now reads the persisted relation) and pinned by `verify.local.dev.data_space_uncached_membership.orm` (4 cases pass on the repair, 4/4 fail on the legacy body). The governed shell lane also announces its own invalidation now (`daily_runtime_lifecycle_fixture_prepare.py`).

target_env_data_space_onboarding_now_present: sc_demo carries the fixture's two owned registrations (company 21 FE Company A and company 22 FE Company B, data_purpose=test, tenant_key=frontend-productization-fixture, active, not platform bootstrap). The FE acceptance records (payment.request 36180/36181) belong to FE Company A and are inside that realm. The demo company 1 records (36029, 1246, project 1246) carry no registration row and stay outside every principal's realm by design, not by defect.

target_env_two_way_isolation_is_not_a_defect: uid 16 (wutao) legitimately lacks the non-customer data group, so its 403 on FE test-space records is the intended customer/non-customer split.
